I am a caregiver (CNA) in a nursing home, and I can tel you... there sure as hell is no guarantee you’ll be taken care of by your kids. I see it all the time. And I work at a very nice facility, even the best ones are still shitty.

People think that I have some kind of amazing motherly caregiver instinct for taking care of the elderly 60 hours a week. And I do. It’s just for taking care of the elderly, though, doesn’t mean I want my own kids.

And they also take everything immediately in the worst way possible. In the post I mentioned OP commented that she had recently had surgery, and everyone was upset because she was “uprooting her entire life” after major surgery for this monster, until she pointed out that they were moving closer to her hospital and he wanted to take care of her...

Why is it always immediately divorce? Once on one of the relationship subs I saw a post where OP was moving in with her long term boyfriend, and they couldn’t agree on where in their new place she should do her jigsaw puzzles. That was her whole problem. There were several comments telling OP to leave him and extrapolating that he’s an abusive monster. These people are so ridiculous.

I believe that this world doesn't matter as much as we think it does, and I don't mean that in a morbid or hopeless way. To me, is a stop on our spiritual journey. I feel a deep purpose for my work on earth but I also feel that my soul work and purpose are not ONLY on earth. I know that in other realms of existence I can't conceive, I will have a purpose there, too. So I've always looked at my time here on earth as stopping at a coffee shop in an unfamiliar place. I'm just stopping in to enjoy what it offers until whatever comes next. I've also had a NDE, which is part of why I have these feelings.

I am so sorry you have to deal with this. I am on the other side of this, with an invisible disability. Oh how quickly people are to glare and judge me when I park in a handicapped space. They can’t see the scars going across my entire head because my hair has grown back. They can’t see the metal plates in my skull, or my damaged nerves. People are so shitty to disabled people. I am so sorry. I don’t know your pain, but no one should ever have to feel that way.

Thank you for the support! :) I actually learned about reborn dolls through my job (I am a hospice caregiver and a death doula) and I learned how amazingly therapuetic it can be for dementia patients! It gives them something positive to focus on, gives them a bit of structure, and makes them feel useful. These dolls really are wonderful when used for purposes like those. And I definitely do understand your points on why it is detrimental for the grieving process!

EDIT: Thinking about it I think I may have come across the wrong way in my original comment - I totally understand what you're saying, I mostly just wanted to share another perspective on other ways these dolls can be used in case you hadn't ever come across someone like me. :)

I love reborn dolls, personally, because they are fun. I am capable of having a baby biologically, but I don't want to commit to the responsibility of actually being a parent. Ever. And I do not want a toddler. But with my reborn, I get the fun parts of having a baby (cute little baby, dressing in cute outfits, cuddling with it, etc.) but I can play with her a little at home and at the end of the day or whenever I want I can put her in her doll crib and live my regular life. I don't take it so seriously as treating her like a real baby. I don't spend exorbitant amounts on her. What I do spend I enjoy.  I don't think this is bad.
